csv_project_name: Design Service for Emergency Operations Center
csv_scope_of_work: The City University of New York (CUNY) is seeking proposals from qualified firms to provide professional assessment, planning, and design services for the development of a Centralized Emergency Operations Center (EOC) at John Jay College of Criminal Justice. Services include evaluating existing conditions and infrastructure, defining operational and technology requirements, developing architectural and engineering designs, preparing technical specifications and supporting documentation, and producing a comprehensive design package for a resilient, scalable, and technology-enabled EOC. The selected consultant will also provide planning-level cost estimates, equipment recommendations, and related advisory services as required.
csv_disciplines_requested: Architecture Services, Interior Design/Space Planning, Programming, Rehabilitation & Refurbishment, Civil Engineering, Surveying/GIS/Mapping
csv_comments: '- Project Number: UCO-1010- Contract Number: 2136995- Contract Participation Goal: Disabled Veteran Owned Business Enterprise- Pre-Submittal Notes: Vendors must RSVP by July 24, 2026, 1:00 PM EST by emailing Adam.Schwartz@cuny.edu. The RSVP must include the attendee’s name, title, company, email address, and phone number. The site visit will take place at 524 W 59th St, New York, NY 10019. Attendees should arrive at least 15 minutes prior to the scheduled start time and bring government-issued photo identification for building access. Because the site visit is mandatory, failure to attend may result in a proposer being deemed non-responsive. Any substantive questions arising from the site visit must be submitted in writing by the applicable deadline. services: Assessment, planning, architectural and engineering design, technical specifications, supporting documentation, planning-level cost estimating, equipment recommendations, advisory services; requested disciplines include architecture, interior design/space planning, programming, rehabilitation/refurbishment, civil engineering, and surveying/GIS/mapping.
relevance_explanation:
- Primarily an interior/building fit-out and emergency operations center project, not a bridge, long-span roof, tower, stadium, or special structure.
- Scope focuses on assessment, planning, architecture, interiors, technology requirements, and refurbishment.
- Civil engineering is listed, but no structurally demanding or innovative load-bearing scope is described.
- Existing-building rehabilitation/refurbishment is generally less relevant for sbp than new complex structures.
- Could involve some building design coordination, but no evidence of significant structural engineering opportunity.
construction_cost_explanation: No construction cost is stated in the source. The notice only mentions that the consultant shall prepare planning-level cost estimates. Useful known information: centralized EOC within an existing college building, resilient and technology-enabled fit-out, 12-month base period, likely refurbishment/adaptation rather than new standalone construction. A realistic cost estimate is not possible from the provided text alone.
fee_explanation: No design fee or budget is stated in the source. The scope covers assessment, planning, architecture/engineering design, specifications, and advisory services for an EOC within an existing facility, but there is insufficient information on area, complexity, or construction budget to derive a reliable fee estimate.
references_qualifications: Qualified firms to provide professional assessment, planning, and design services for the EOC. Specific reference counts or detailed qualification thresholds are not stated in the provided text. Mandatory site visit attendance is required; failure to attend may render a proposer non-responsive.
